data.title: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.

sections.explain: 'Can' is used for ability and is followed by the base verb.

sections.sentence: You ___ bring your passport to the airport.
I ___ go to work tomorrow because I have a meeting.
sections.explain: 'Have to' is used when something is required by circumstances.

sections.sentence: You ___ study more if you want to pass the exam.
sections.explain: 'Should' expresses advice and is followed by the base verb.

sections.sentence: She ___ attend the meeting because she is sick.
sections.explain: 'Can't' shows inability and is followed by the base verb.
'Mustn't' expresses that something is not allowed.

sections.sentence: You ___ buy a ticket online if you prefer.
We ___ wake up early tomorrow for our journey.
sections.summary: Use 'have to' for required future plans.
sections.explain: 'Have to' expresses obligation due to plans or rules.

sections.sentence: You ___ bring food; we already have dinner ready.
sections.summary: Use 'don't have to' for no obligation.
sections.explain: 'Don't have to' means something is not necessary.

sections.sentence: She ___ apologize because it was not her mistake.
sections.summary: Use 'doesn't have to' for no obligation (third person).
sections.explain: With 'she', use 'doesn't have to' to show no obligation.
